$comment: Table ownership for the modular-monolith slices. One module owns each table and is the
only thing that may write it; `readableBy` lists the modules that may SELECT it.
This file is the source, not a mirror: `pnpm gen:grants` turns it into
`db/grants.generated.sql` (one `module_<name>` Postgres role each) and into
`packages/core/src/kernel/db.modules.generated.ts`. `db:migrate` applies the SQL after
`prisma migrate deploy`, and the kernel's `db.tx(module, fn)` runs `SET LOCAL ROLE
module_<name>`, so a write to a foreign table is refused by the database itself.
Names are TABLE names (the Prisma `@@map` value), not model names. The two differ
throughout: `WhatsAppConnection` maps to `whatsapp_connection`.
`readableBy` is `"*"` everywhere for now. Narrowing one is a deliberate act: every read
the removed module still makes will start failing with `permission denied` the moment the
grants are regenerated, which is the point.
Derivation and the one judgement call are recorded in
openspec/changes/adopt-modular-vertical-slices/tasks.md section 1.1 (correction C1).

accounts.description: Units, users and the unit membership that scopes every other module's reads.

channel.description: The WhatsApp transport. The only module that talks to Evolution, and the only writer of the outbound queue.

conversations.description: Threads, their messages, the tags and templates applied to them, and follow-up bookkeeping.

customers.description: Customers, their contact rows and vehicles, plus the ERP field-sync and reconciliation state for both.

prefill.description: Assistive cadastro extraction: the job queue and the suggestions an attendant accepts or rejects.

services.description: Services performed and their items, the vehicle-return dates computed from them, and the interval rules those dates are computed with.

scheduling.description: Deferred sends: scheduled messages and the return reminders that produce them.

quotes.description: Oil quotes and the catalog and compatibility data they are priced from.

plate-lookup.description: Plate lookups and the per-call ledger the provider is billed against.

reports.description: Attribution: the rule in force and the per-service attributions computed under it.

erp.description: The ERP transport. Pull bookkeeping, integration errors, and the write-back queue for the two-way ERP.

$comment: Paths that write across module lines by design and must NOT be given contracts.
They run as the login role, which is a member of every module role and so strictly
more capable than any of them; their own writes do not go through `db.tx`, so no grant
applies to them. One exception: the demo seed opens vehicle returns by calling services'
reconcileVehicleReturns contract, which runs under db.tx with module roles, so seeding
needs the grants `pnpm db:migrate` applies.
Seeds build a whole world, the scrub deletes across two modules on purpose, and the
rollback harness seeds under the login role because design.md D2 requires it.
The role test asserts nothing under packages/core/src/modules/ is listed here.
